footer.about: A curation and reputation market for Solana, built by PixStock. The ranking is bought with exposed capital, and lost with it.
legal: Not advice. Nothing here is investment advice, an offer, or a solicitation.
Total loss is possible. Staking exposes capital to slashing, up to the whole stake.
The guarantee fund is not insurance. Compensation is capped at 40 % of the observed loss and at the fund’s available balance, paid pro rata, with no guarantee of completeness.
Challenge is not settled. It awaits a written legal opinion and will be geo-restricted where required.

home.statement: Trust becomes a measurable asset instead of a claim.

problem.title: Discovery sells the first place. It never earns it.
problem.lede: Solana produces tens of thousands of new tokens a day, and aggregators sell the first place at ad rates.

slides.title: Information asymmetry
slides.body: Liquidity lock, mint authority, deployer history: the fields that decide whether a token survives. None of them is on the page. The price is.
slides.alt: A token page where every risk field is blanked out and only the price is legible

slides.kicker: At the top of the list
slides.title: Venal visibility
slides.body: The ranking rewards the marketing budget, including that of a scammer preparing an exit. First place is a media buy.
slides.alt: A ranking whose first place is a paid placement, sitting above the honest rows

slides.title: Issuer impunity
slides.body: The pool empties into the deployer’s own wallet, the page stays up, and the next token launches from the same address.
slides.alt: A liquidity pool draining into the deployer wallet with no consequence attached

slides.title: Reputation resets
slides.body: A caller’s record lives on social media: declarative, unauditable, wiped with every new account. Being wrong costs nothing.
slides.alt: Three wallets in a row, each with a score of zero, and a loop back to a fresh one

mechanicSection.title: Two sides. Both of them pay to be wrong.
mechanicSection.lede: Not volume, not a media buy: locked capital, weighted by the reputation of whoever locked it.

boost.title: Stake to Boost
boost.claim: Lock capital to assert that a token is not fraudulent and will survive the round.
boost.outcomeRight: Stake returned in full, a share of the slashed pot, reputation points.
boost.outcomeWrong: Graduated slashing per the schedule below, and reputation destroyed.

challenge.title: Challenge
challenge.claim: Lock capital to flag that a token shows the signature of fraud or imminent collapse.
challenge.outcomeRight: Stake returned, 70 % of the slashed pot shared pro rata, vigilance points.
challenge.outcomeWrong: Flat 30 % of the stake forfeited to the buyer guarantee fund.

mechanicSection.note: Challenge capital is subtractive, so a contested token falls in the ranking before it is ever resolved. That is the visitor’s protection in real time.
mechanicSection.more: Weight formula, resolution ladder, slashing schedule

round.lede: Stakes are accepted for two hours only. After that, positions are frozen and nobody enters or exits.

meta.title: The Rule Set
meta.description: How a position is priced, judged, slashed and paid: the ranking weight formula, the resolution ladder, the slashing schedule and the reputation gates.

pageHead.lede: What a position is worth, how it is judged, and what it costs to be wrong.

weight.title: Rank is capital, multiplied by a reputation you had to earn.
weight.lede: Not a score the platform assigns: the sum of what everyone locked, each stake scaled by reputation and lock duration, minus the capital against it.
weight.tableCaption: Ranking weight | how a position is priced

rows.def: Sum of stake × reputation multiplier × duration factor, minus challenge capital
Applied to challenge capital, subtracted from weight

weight.note: The 0.6 coefficient stops a small coalition from burying an honest project cheaply.

resolution.title: Fraud is examined before price, and stops the round on the spot.
paragraphs: An honest memecoin routinely loses half its value in a day. Punishing that would leave only the manipulators.
Structural fraud is examined first. Price enters second, as a volume-weighted average.

rows.criterion: Deployer or a linked wallet pulls more than 50 % of liquidity
Mint or freeze authority exercised during the round
Deployer or linked wallet sells more than 40 % of its balance
Swaps become impossible, prohibitive sell tax, active blacklist
Liquidity collapses more than 70 % without deployer action
Volume-weighted price over the last two hours vs. the T0 reference

resolution.note: Ranks 1 to 4 are checked continuously and resolve the round on the spot, before the platform can hold a fraud in first place.

slashing.title: What a wrong call costs, stated before you sign.
slashing.lede: A drawdown of up to 20 % costs nothing: honest volatility is not a fraud. Past that the schedule is graduated, and characterised fraud takes everything.
slashing.tableCaption: Slashing applied to the Boost stake
slashing.note: The schedule is shown and acknowledged before signature, never deferred to the terms of service.

pot.title: The treasury takes a handling fee, not a rent on fraud.
paragraphs: There is an obvious objection to any platform that collects a cut of slashing: it makes money when its users get scammed.
Sending the bulk to the people who flagged the risk and the buyers who lost is what answers it. The burn makes self-hedging loss-making.

bars.label: Challenge positions
bars.why: Pro rata to the stakes that called it, paid on the resolved round.

bars.label: Buyer guarantee fund
bars.why: Partial compensation for wallets that bought through the widget, capped at 40 % of the loss.

bars.label: Permanent burn
bars.why: Makes hedging your own Boost with your own Challenge a losing trade. See RG-06.

pot.note: Compensation is capped and pro rata, stated in the interface rather than buried.

reputation.title: An identity worth faking has to cost more than the fraud it enables.
paragraphs: A 0-1000 score that multiplies the weight of every SOL you stake, rebuilt from on-chain transactions and public to anyone.
It cannot be bought in one round: a high multiplier is gated on cumulative capital exposed, resolved rounds and account age. One characterised fraud sends it to zero, permanently flagged.

gates.caption: Opening score of 100. Every new wallet starts here.
Gated on 50 SOL cumulative exposure across at least 15 resolved rounds.
Gated on 300 SOL across 60 resolved rounds and 90 days of account age.
Weekly decay with no resolved round. Floor at 100.

reputation.chartAriaLabel: Reputation multiplier curve: 0.5 times at a score of zero, rising linearly to 3.0 times at a score of 1000, where it is capped.
reputation.note: Reputation gained is capped by the capital that wallet has historically exposed, so one large winning round buys nothing.

pageHead.h1: Three lots, 36 weeks, two hard gates.
pageHead.lede: Nothing financial ships on optimism. Each lot waits on a gate that is written down.

roadmap.lotsTitle: Audience first. Money on the line only after the legal opinion.

lots.goal: Build the index and the organic traffic first, and show issuers measured traffic for free.
bullets: Automatic listing of every SPL token with an active pair
Token pages, security panel, non-staked rankings
Swap widget with a 0.75 % routing fee

lots.goal: Introduce Boost against a program reduced to escrow. Resolution stays off-chain so the rules can still be iterated.
bullets: Escrow program, position opening, internal pricing
lots.block: written legal opinion, two independent program audits. Total value locked capped at 300 SOL for the first four weeks.

lots.goal: Open the sell side in its validated form, move the distribution cascade on-chain, ship position copying.
lots.block: rug rate inside the top 10 held under 12 % for eight consecutive weeks.

targets.title: One number decides whether any of this worked.
paragraphs: The rug rate inside the top 10 is the cardinal indicator. It is the only one that measures whether the mechanic does what it claims.
It counts tokens that held a top-10 position for six hours or more, observed for seven days after they leave.
targets.note: Revenue is 78 % routing fees, so the whole model is correlated to Solana memecoin volume, a cyclical base. Every projection is carried alongside a low case at a quarter of the volume.

compliance.title: The gates are written down, so they cannot be quietly moved.
paragraphs: Paying people to correctly predict a collapse touches prediction-market and market-abuse rules that differ by jurisdiction. That is not an engineering question, so it is not treated as one.
The escrow program is the only component holding user funds, and the only one audited twice before it sees real capital.

rows.d: Two firms on the escrow program, 60 000 to 120 000 USD, provisioned from Lot 1. Blocking prerequisite to Lot 2.
Required on the Challenge side before Lot 2. Lot 3 ships only the variant it validates.
Multi-signature through Lot 2, frozen at Lot 3. Rule changes pass through a parameter update, never unversioned code.
Limited to 300 SOL for the first four weeks of Lot 2, raised in steps only after an incident-free period.
Applied where the local qualification of Challenge requires it.
Kept strictly outside the staked ranking, visually distinct and labelled. 2 % of expected revenue. Blending the two would destroy the only thing the product sells.

meta.title: Objections
meta.description: Manipulation, whales, custody, the legal position on the Challenge side, and where the revenue comes from. The hard questions about staked curation, answered.

pageHead.h1: The hard questions, answered in the open.
pageHead.lede: A mechanic that takes people’s money has to survive its objections in public. These are the six that matter.

qa.q: Why would anyone Boost, if the downside is a slashed stake?
a: Because the upside is not the price of the token. It is the pot. A correct Boost gets its stake back in full, takes a share of the capital slashed from wrong positions elsewhere, and gains reputation that permanently multiplies the weight of every future stake.
A normal drawdown of up to 20 % is not slashed at all. That threshold exists precisely so honest volatility is not punished.

qa.q: What stops a whale from simply buying first place?
a: Nothing stops them trying, and that is the point: rank costs exposure for the full round with no exit after two hours, not budget.
Weight is capped by reputation too: fresh capital carries a 0.75× multiplier, and challenge capital is subtracted.

qa.q: Can a curator manipulate the price of a thin pair to win?
a: This is the model’s primary threat, and the reason resolution is hierarchical rather than price-only. Any deployer or linked-wallet action (liquidity pulled, authority exercised, balance dumped) is examined before price and resolves as characterised fraud with a 100 % slash.
Price only settles the ranks below that, and linked-wallet detection feeds the same graph used to exclude wash volume.

qa.q: Is the Challenge side legally settled?
a: No. Paying people to correctly predict a collapse touches prediction-market and market-abuse rules that differ by jurisdiction. A written legal opinion is a hard gate before Lot 2, and the sell side ships in Lot 3 only in the variant it validates.

No custody of keys, and no custody of funds beyond the stake escrow itself. Swaps route through a third-party aggregator; the escrow program handles locking, release, slashing and distribution, and nothing else.
Yes, kept strictly outside the staked ranking: a separate placement, visually distinct, labelled as sponsored. Blending the two would destroy the only thing this product sells.

faq.note: The one question still open is the qualification of the Challenge side, and that is deliberate.
